target_customer: Consumers who want social video hangouts with friends rather than meetings
problem: Video chat was built for meetings; Rume recreated the feel of an in-person event where people move between smaller conversations.
business_model: Consumer social video app (monetization not described in sources)

founders.name: Ben Scharfstein
prior_employers: Google (associate product manager, Android and Search)
founders.background_notes: YC page: researched the structure of social networks at Harvard.

founders.name: Vincenzo (Cenzo) Vitiello
founders.background_notes: No education or employers on the YC page.

founders.name: Bryant Wolf
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked in legal tech, pharma, crypto-finance, security and authentication, and the on-demand economy.

exit.reason: The company site says the service is closed after about two years; no cause is stated

competitors.name: Houseparty
competitors.what: Group video chat app with virtual rooms, owned by Epic Games
competitors.traction_then: Company claimed about 200 million users by March 2020, up from about 10 million in December 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time multi-room video built on WebRTC is standard but needs care for latency and scale.

defensibility.rationale: Social video could develop network effects, but Zoom, Houseparty and later spatial chat tools offered similar experiences and features were easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large platforms added social video features during 2020; no one acquired Rume.

market_need_then: COVID lockdowns in 2020 created a surge in video calling and a demand for social alternatives to meeting software, per 2020 coverage of Houseparty.

identity.voice_and_tone: Grateful and nostalgic in the closing message; tagline Video chat that doesn't feel like work

branding.brand_signature: Tagline Video chat that doesn't feel like work
branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt launches including an Among Us integration; games such as Codenames and Settlers of Catan; Twitter and Instagram accounts under rumevideo.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear tagline and a friendly short name, but little press or community evidence.

outcome_analysis: Rume was a three-person social video chat startup in Summer 2020 that raised a small seed and ran for roughly two years before the site announced the service closed. No post-mortem or cause was found, so no failure factors are assigned. Zoom, Houseparty and spatial chat tools were crowded rivals, but their effect on Rume is not sourced.
notes: CB Insights reports $130K raised over 3 rounds with the latest a seed dated August 25, 2020 (investors Y Combinator, South Park Commons, Catapult VC); the page could not be opened directly, so the round rests on a search snippet from a single database and its amount is not recorded. The site footer credits Lume Social Inc (2021) and one aggregator says Lume Social operated Rume, unverified. The Houseparty source URL carries no date; the traction figure is a 2020 claim. Shutdown date not stated. Cause is not public. Later rivals Kumospace and Gather are excluded as they came after the batch.
